'''Gerhard Ludwig Closs''' (May 1, 1928 &ndash; May 24, 1992) was an American chemist specializing in [[physical organic chemistry]],<ref name="NYT">[https://www.nytimes.com/1992/06/05/obituaries/gerhard-closs-is-dead-pioneering-chemist-64.html New York Times:Gerhard Closs Is Dead; Pioneering Chemist, 64]</ref> member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] and the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]],<ref name="NAP">[http://www.nap.edu/openbook.php?record_id=10992&page=53 National Academies Press:GERHARD LUDWIG CLOSS, BY HEINZ D. ROTH]</ref> chairman of the chemistry department at the University of Chicago.<ref name="NYT"/>
<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/1974/04/28/archives/science-academy-elects-96-members.html?sq=%2522Gerhard%2520Ludwig%2520Closs%2522&scp=1&st=cse New York Times:Science Academy Elects 96 Members, April 28, 1974], </ref>
Closs made seminal contributions in research of  the magnetic properties of the intermediate compounds formed in chemical reactions.<ref name="NYT"/>
He is also credited with the discovery that certain reactions polarize atomic nuclei.<ref name="NYT"/>
The [[National Academies Press]] called him "one of the outstanding chemists of the post-World War II era".<ref name="NAP"/>
He was also an early leader in the field of carbene chemistry.<ref name="NAP"/>
The [[New York Times]] called him "pioneering chemist".<ref name="NYT"/>

== Awards and Distinctions ==
* Jean Servas Stas Medal by the Belgian Chemical Society in 1971<ref name="NAP"/>
* James Flack Norris award by the [[American Chemical Society]] in 1974<ref name="NAP"/>
* [[Arthur C. Cope Award]] by the [[American Chemical Society]] in 1991<ref name="NAP"/>
* Photochemistry Prize by the Inter-American Photochemical Association in 1992<ref name="NAP"/>
* elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1974<ref name="NAP"/>
* elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1975<ref name="NAP"/>
* The Inter-American Photochemical Association honors his memory with the G. L. Closs Memorial Award<ref name="NAP"/>
